description: Canonical-form step 3: term ordering, collation, and positive-before-negative grouping.

cases.rationale: Terms sort by symbol, not by the order the producer wrote them.

Bytewise UTF-8 collation puts every uppercase-initial symbol before every lowercase-initial one. A case-folding collation would produce Btu*h*kW*m*MW*W — a different string, and therefore a different hash, for the same expression. This case is the whole reason AMB-003 has to be decided rather than assumed.
Two units differing only by case must have a defined order. 'M' (0x4D) sorts before 'm' (0x6D) bytewise.
One symbol is a proper prefix of another. Bytewise comparison puts the shorter first, so m precedes mW.
All positive-exponent terms precede all negative-exponent terms regardless of source order. Under the decided canonical form (AMB-001: no slashes on output) the sign renders in the exponent itself.
The negative terms sort among themselves: K (0x4B) before m (0x6D) bytewise. Also note length cancels to zero and is omitted from the dimension vector entirely.

One positive and one negative term; grouping alone fixes the order, so no collation question arises. Also exercises §6.2's currency base dimension — USD/MWh parses and propagates even though §2 forbids cross-currency conversion.
